explanation: The downstream priorities lost upstream provenance rank: every priority has upstream_rank 0. The downstream prioritize function looks up evidence_sources by record_id, so the handoff must contain record identities compatible with need record_id values. Job 1's assemble_provenance instead emits evidence_sources record_id values as source IDs (s01, s02, etc.), making them impossible to match to coverage record IDs like n06-r01. This breaks the requirement to preserve upstream provenance order into the downstream ranking.
cited_evidence: Job 1 needs preserve demand record IDs such as n06-r01 through n06-r08, while Job 1 evidence_sources emit record_id values s01 through s08.
The source code for assemble_provenance sets "record_id": record.get('source_id', "") instead of preserving the demand record_id.
Job 2 prioritize builds rank_by_record_id from evidence_sources record_id and then looks up coverage.get("record_id"), so the mismatched IDs produce upstream_rank 0 for every observed priority.
Observed Job 2 priorities show upstream_rank: 0 on all eight records, violating the criterion to preserve upstream provenance order.
